bib.title: ASQA: Factoid Questions Meet Long-Form Answers

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "ASQA: Factoid Questions Meet Long-Form Answers". Ivan Stelmakh, Yi Luan, Bhuwan Dhingra, Ming-Wei Chang (Google Research, Duke, Yakov & Partners). Published in the Proceedings of EMNLP 2022, pages 8273–8288. The PDF is the ACL Anthology proceedings version, not the arXiv preprint. arXiv 2204.06092. 2022.

COVERAGE: I read all 65,161 of 65,161 characters across 16 pages. That covers the body, Limitations (§9), Appendices A–C and Table 6. I skimmed the reference list for origins. Page numbers below are PDF pages; printed page = 8272 + PDF page. Figures were checked with figures.py captions.

SUGGESTED HOME IN THE NOTE: `generative-ai/02-rag-retrieval/notes/06-generation-for-rag.md`, section "## Evaluating the generator: RAGAS" (around line 391). DR is a non-LLM-judge counterpoint to RAGAS: answerability by a QA model, combined with ROUGE-L. It also shows the recall-only blind spot. The Table 6 error analysis (hallucination, mixed-up sources, on-topic but not answering) could go under "## Hallucinations and citations" as a short sharpening. The finding that T5 loses information present in the retrieved passages (Fig. 3) could support "## Order and size of the context".

CLAIMS
- claim: The DR score is the geometric mean of Disambig-F1 and ROUGE-L. It was chosen so a system cannot max one metric at the cost of the other.
  number: DR = sqrt(Disambig-F1 × ROUGE-L)
  setup: ASQA dev/test, multi-reference ROUGE-L (max over two annotator answers)
  quote: "DR = √ Disambig-F1 × ROUGE-L. We choose the geometric mean for aggregation to penalize methods that maximize one metric at a cost of the other."
  where: p6 (8278)
- claim: Disambig-F1 runs a RoBERTa reader trained on SQuADv2 over the generated long answer. It asks each disambiguated question from AmbigQA, scores token-level F1 against the gold short answer, and averages within each question and then across questions.
  number: none
  setup: HuggingFace scripts; SQuADv2 answer normalisation
  quote: "use Roberta (Liu et al., 2019) trained on SQUADV2 to evaluate the fraction of disambiguated questions that can be answered from the predicted long answers."
  where: p6 (8278)
- claim: DR has the highest Pearson correlation with the overall human judgment (HO) of any automated metric. Its edge over Disambig-F1 alone is not statistically significant.
  number: HO correlation: ROUGE-L 86.4, Disambig-F1 92.9, DR 95.0. ACC correlation: 81.1 / 99.3 / 97.9
  setup: 4 systems plus 2 human sets, 45 random dev questions, pairwise judgments by the paper's own authors, blind
  quote: "HO 86.4 92.9 95.0" / "ACC 81.1 99.3 97.9" / "While the difference with Disambig-F1 is not statistically significant"
  where: p9 (8281, Table 5) and p8 (8280)
- claim: Retrieval matters. Open-book T5 beats closed-book T5 by a wide margin, and random retrieved passages collapse performance. The authors contrast this with ELI5.
  number: T5-O-1 +12.8 DR, +20.0 HO; T5-O-5 +17.0 DR, +15.6 HO; random retrieval DR 7.8
  setup: T5-large; JPR passages; dev set

HP-w/-C: 49.4*/98.4/77.4/61.8*. (*ROUGE-L against one reference only.)

LIMITS
- The authors concede that the accuracy metrics measure recall only. A hallucinated extra disambiguation or fact may not be penalised, except indirectly through ROUGE-L and reader distraction. Quote: "our accuracy metrics (STR-EM and Disambig-F1) only measure the recall of the required information in the long answers. In cases where the long answer hallucinates incorrect disambiguations or facts, the accuracy metrics may still be high" (p9, 8281).
- The authors concede that agreement may be inflated, because both annotators shared the AmbigQA disambiguations.
- The authors concede that Disambig-F1 needs a high-accuracy QA reader. Outside Wikipedia, the RoBERTa SQuADv2 model may need fine-tuning.
- The human correlation study is tiny: 45 questions and 6 systems. The judges were the paper's own authors.
- The paper does not measure precision or faithfulness to retrieved passages. Citation or attribution of the generated output is not measured either.
- This has dated. The baselines are T5-large and DPR/JPR from 2022, with no LLMs. Most correlations are over 6 systems, so a Pearson r across systems has very few points.
- The data is Wikipedia-only and the questions are NQ-derived factoid questions.

BUILDS ON: AmbigQA (Min et al., 2020); JPR (Min et al., 2021); DPR (Karpukhin et al., 2020); T5 (Raffel et al., 2019); closed-book QA (Roberts et al., 2020); ROUGE (Lin, 2004); SQuAD / SQuADv2 (Rajpurkar et al., 2016, 2018); RoBERTa (Liu et al., 2019); ELI5 (Fan et al., 2019); hurdles in long-form QA, including the random-retrieval baseline (Krishna et al., 2021); QA-based factual-consistency evaluation (Wang et al., 2020; Durmus et al., 2020; Honovich et al., 2021); WebGPT (Nakano et al., 2021); NQ-open (Kwiatkowski et al., 2019; Lee et al., 2019); distractors (Jia and Liang, 2017).

CODE: The paper has no code. The repo it cites is github.com/google-research/language/tree/master/language/asqa (p2). The metric formula, verbatim, is "Disambig-F1 = 1N ∑k 1n(k) ∑i ϕ(ˆy(k)i , y(k)i )" (p6). A cleaner rendering is (1/N) Σ_k (1/n_k) Σ_i F1(ŷ_i^k, y_i^k).

FIGURES
- Figure 1 (p2) is the best candidate for the note. Caption: "The input questions in ASQA are sourced from AMBIGQA. Long-form answers must be sufficient to answer disambiguated questions from AMBIGQA ... The DR score we propose combines ROUGE and Disambiguation-accuracy (Disambig-Acc) metrics". It shows the whole metric in one picture: the ambiguous question (ruler of France in 1830), two disambiguations, max over references for ROUGE, mean over questions for accuracy, and the geometric mean.
- Figure 3 (p9) is a second option. Caption: "Disambig-F1 of different methods with a varying number of retrieved passages. ... there is also an increasing gap between T5-O-K and JPR@K." It shows at a glance that the generator drops information it was given.
- Figure 2 (annotation interface) and Figures 4–5 (input formats) are lower value. Figures 4–5 extracted as captions only.

PROBLEMS: Table columns extracted with split decimals (e.g. "39 .2 41 .0"). I read them as 39.2 and 41.0, and they are consistent with the prose. Figure 1 text extracted out of order. The Figure 4/5 input-format schematics did not extract as text. The PDF contains no embedded instructions.
